claims.source_quote_ar: فما بال التعمد مشروطاً في الآية؟
claims.claim_ar: مقابلة بين الإباحة (أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ) والتحريم (وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ) لبيان التمييز الشرعي بين حالتي البحر والبر
claims.claim_en: A rhetorical contrast (muqabalah) between the permissibility of sea catch and the prohibition of land catch, highlighting the legal distinction between the two situations.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted passage discusses the ayah's legal context (إحرام) rather than explicitly naming the rhetorical device; the identification of 'contrast' is interpretive.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار لفظ المخاطبة (لَكُمْ ... لَكُمْ) كوسيلة بلاغية للتأكيد أو التخصيص
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the addressee particle (lakum ... lakum) functions rhetorically to emphasize or to specify the addressed group.
claims.needs_review_reason: Support is analogical: the source chunk gives a general example of repetition for emphasis; the application to this specific particle in the ayah is plausible but not directly discussed in the chunk.

claims.source_quote_ar: محظورات الإحرام يستوي فيها العمد والخطأ
claims.claim_ar: اقتصار تحريم صَيْدِ البَرِّ على حالة الإحرام (مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا) — أي أن التحريم مقرون بزمن الإحرام فقط
claims.claim_en: The prohibition of land hunting is restricted to the period of ihram ('ma dumtum huruman'); the ban applies only while one remains in the state of ihram.

claims.claim_ar: اتحاد الشرط والجزاء في عبارة (مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا)؛ أي أن الجزاء (القيود أو الأحكام) مرتبط حضورياً بشرط دوام الحالة المذكورة
claims.claim_en: Union of condition and consequence: in 'ma dumtum huruman' the consequence (the legal effect) is presented as inseparable from the stated condition (the state of ihram).
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted comment treats the general rhetorical/legal phenomenon of union between condition and consequence; applying it to this particular clause is reasonable but interpretive.
